sara.dev: Heads-up — legal escalated a DSAR for erasure. User requests full deletion of chat logs + embeddings tied to user_id U-8421. They specifically called out backups in GCS and asked if keys are rotated when we purge.
ravi.sec: ack. Can you drop the DSAR ID and whether identity proof is complete? also need to know region (EU/US).
sara.dev: DSAR-2026-114, identity verified (gov ID). Region: EU. They want a confirm once everything (including backups/snapshots) is removed.
legal.ops: confirmed identity. DSAR scope: all PII-derived artifacts and embeddings associated with U-8421 across hosted and dedicated. No legal hold.
mike.ml: deleting embeddings only is straightforward in vector-db, but backups/snapshots may still contain rows. Need to check snapshot retention + encryption key lifecycle.
eden.infra: snapshot retention for embeddings indices is 60d in GCS (eu-west-1 bucket). Backups are encrypted with platform KMS key rk-platform-1. We rotate keys on schedule, but rotation doesn't remove older ciphertexts — deleting ciphertext requires object deletion or re-encryption and reupload.
ravi.sec: sounds like we need to treat this as a retention-exception workflow: 1) identify all storage locations 2) remove vectors and metadata 3) list and delete backup objects / snapshots 4) verify KMS logs for decrypt operations. Also need to lock RBAC so only a small SRE group can perform deletions.
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1145 (type: DSAR erasure, priority: P1)
sara.dev: I'm running the lookup now — running `python tools/find_user_artifacts.py --user U-8421 --team all` and will paste results.
[sara.dev pasted output snippet]
```
vector_db: eu-vectors/idx-7 entries: 1243 objects matched
gcs: gs://rwd-embeddings-eu/snapshots/2026-02-12/manifest.json (contains user refs)
logs: stackdriver: logs/user-U-8421/**
```
eden.infra: ok. Plan: 1) take final snapshot (retention off) 2) delete user rows from vector index 3) delete snapshots + manifests referencing U-8421 4) request KMS audit dump for keys used on those objects.
mike.ml: small note — deleting rows may change index layout. We'll run the post-delete eval to ensure no model regressions on production prompt set.
legal.ops: confirm we need an auditable trail + timestamped proof of deletion sent to requester.
ravi.sec: on RBAC: I'll create a short-lived role `dsar-erasure-operator` with `gcs.objects.delete`, `vectordb.delete`, and `kms.viewAudit` scoped to the resources, TTL 8h. Only assign to eden.infra and ravi.sec.
sara.dev: timeline? we need to respond to user within 30 days.
eden.infra: I can do the deletion run tomorrow 09:00 UTC. I'll run a dry-run first and post results.
sec-bot: Reminder: add retention-exception flag and update compliance ticket CNF-4287.
mike.ml: action: I'll prepare the evaluation notebook and run it against canary after deletion. ETA 3h post-delete.
ravi.sec: also need to rotate service account keys that had `vectordb-admin` perms as a precaution. I'll open a short PR to change the role binding.
legal.ops: once you have the proof-of-deletion artifact (manifest of deleted object names + storage deletion timestamps + KMS audit export), send to DSAR-2026-114 and cc:privacy@redwood.com.
sara.dev: copying plan into the DSAR ticket now. tagging @eden.infra for the run and @ravi.sec for RBAC changes.
eden.infra: starting dry-run now, will post the truncated logs here in ~15m.
ravi.sec: tagging this for follow-up: update runbook to cover "EU DSAR with backups in GCS" — note: ensure KMS audit export TTL is long enough for legal review.
sara.dev: thanks all. will close loop after proofs are uploaded.
sec-bot: INC-2026-1145 status -> in_progress (assignees: eden.infra, ravi.sec)
